subject: physics_2
question_text: Classify the following materials with regard to magnetism: Manganese, Cobalt, Nickel, Bismuth, Oxygen, Copper.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: cobalt and nickel are ferromagnetic (with iron and gadolinium); manganese and oxygen are paramagnetic (small positive χ); bismuth and copper are diamagnetic (small negative χ) — the book's classification of all six is correct.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ferro and para
steps.margin_note: First mark. One labelled line per material — the examiner reads the pairs at a glance.
steps.why: Cobalt and nickel are two of the classic ferromagnetic elements (iron, cobalt, nickel, gadolinium). Manganese and oxygen have a small positive susceptibility, so they are paramagnetic.
common_mistakes: Calling manganese ferromagnetic because it sits near iron in the periodic table. Manganese is paramagnetic.
Calling oxygen non-magnetic. Oxygen is paramagnetic — liquid oxygen sticks between magnet poles.

recall.must_convey: That cobalt and nickel are ferromagnetic while manganese and oxygen are paramagnetic.

steps.memory_tip: The magnet metals are iron, cobalt, nickel — so cobalt and nickel go under ferromagnetic.

steps.label: Dia
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Bismuth and copper are the two diamagnetic materials in the list.
steps.why: Bismuth and copper have a small negative susceptibility — a magnet feebly repels them — which is the mark of a diamagnetic material.
common_mistakes: Calling copper paramagnetic because it conducts well. Electrical conduction and magnetism are separate properties — copper is diamagnetic.

recall.must_convey: That bismuth and copper are diamagnetic.

steps.memory_tip: Bismuth is the strongest common diamagnetic material, and copper joins it — both are feebly repelled.

insider_note: Write six labelled lines, one material each — a paragraph mixing the six names is where the examiner loses the pairs.
